'''Saimin''' (from Cantonese Chinese:  細麵, sai³ min⁶, thin (wheat) noodles, or 細麵條湯 sai³ min⁶ tiu⁵ tong¹, vermicelli soup) is a [[noodle soup]] dish common in the contemporary [[cuisine of Hawaii]]. Traditionally consisting of soft wheat egg [[noodle]]s served in a hot {{Transliteration|ja|[[dashi]]}} garnished with diced [[Scallion|green onions]] and a thin slice of {{Transliteration|ja|[[kamaboko]]}}, modern versions of saimin include additional toppings such as ''[[char siu]]'', sliced [[Spam (food)|Spam]], [[egg garnish|sliced egg]], [[bok choy]], [[mushroom]]s, or shredded [[nori]]. When [[wontons]] are added to the noodle soup, it is seen on menus as the heartier ''wonton min''. All saimin establishments have their own, often secret recipe for the soup base, but primarily use {{Transliteration|ja|[[kombu]]}} and [[dried shrimp]] as major ingredients. Common [[Condiment|table condiments]] mixed in the saimin broth are [[Mustard (condiment)|Chinese hot mustard]] and [[soy sauce]], added in small quantities according to each individual's taste. Many local residents of Hawaii also enjoy barbecued [[teriyaki]] beef sticks ([[Kebab|skewers]]) or [[Hamburger|American hamburgers]] as a side dish.

Saimin was developed during Hawaii's [[Sugar plantations in Hawaii|plantation era]] and is a testament to the history of cultural influences found in the [[Hawaiian Islands]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archives |first=L. A. Times |date=1993-06-06 |title=A Sample of Saimin Can Be... |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-06-06-tr-131-story.html |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> It is a local [[comfort food]] eaten all year round at any time of day for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or as a late-night snack. Initially consumed by the [[working class]], saimin can now be seen on the menus of Hawaii's restaurants from [[Fast food restaurant|fast food chains]] to upscale [[five-star hotel]] restaurants. It is commonly eaten at sporting events or available precooked [[Convenience food|packaged food]] much like [[Instant noodle|instant ramen]].
